turns.content: Hey, so I wrote a draft apology letter to Sam. It's almost our anniversary Friday and I'm kinda freaking out 😬. Could you take a look? I think it's pretty good but I'm too close to it now.
I’ll pull up your draft and any context about Sam so I can read it the way they might. 💌

Okay, here it is. Be brutal but gentle? 😬


*To Sam,*

*I know I hurt you. I know I pulled away when you needed me most, and I am so, so sorry for the pain I caused. I've been doing a lot of thinking, and I need to try to explain—not to excuse it, but so you know what was going on in my head. I was so burned out from work, and honestly panicking about money, and I think sometimes you misinterpreted my exhaustion as coldness or disinterest. It wasn't that.*

*I miss you. I miss our late-night talks and the way you'd laugh at my stupid jokes.*

*All my love,*
*Taylor*
I’ll check what I already know about you and Sam so the notes on this letter actually fit the situation. 💌

ugh okay but like... isn't total transparency the whole point of an apology? *sweats nervously* if I just say "sorry I was distant" without explaining why, doesn't that feel hollow? 😅

what if I add a really heartfelt memory at the start to soften it? like:

*"I keep thinking about that night we stayed up till 3am building that terrible IKEA furniture and laughing so hard we cried. I miss that so much it physically hurts."*

then the rest. does that balance it better? or should I also promise something big? like a weekend away or cooking their favorite meal? *cries in corner* I just want this to feel real to them
I’ll look back at what you’ve already told me about you and Sam so this advice actually matches the situation, not generic apology-letter tips. 💌

Okay but now I'm just spiraling that if I tone down the explanations it'll sound like I'm hiding from the real issues? 😬 Like if I just say "sorry I was cold" without the burnout context, won't Sam think I was cold for no reason?? That feels worse??
I’ll check what you’ve already shared about you and Sam so this doesn’t turn into generic apology advice. 💌
